title: The Adaptive Cognition Framework: Integrating Evolution, Neurodevelopment, and Metabolic Constraint to Understand Neurodiversity and Inform Educational Practice
content: Neurodevelopmental conditions like autism and ADHD are traditionally viewed as deficits. However, evolutionary neuroscience and brain energetics suggest a more nuanced interpretation. Evolutionary innovations such as cortical expansion and prolonged development enhanced human cognitive flexibility but heightened developmental sensitivity. Consequently, neurodivergent brains exhibit alternative structural organisation and connectivity that operate under finite metabolic constraints, directly shaping cognitive performance and learning. Integrating this evidence, this paper proposes the Adaptive Cognition Framework (ACF). The ACF conceptualises neurodiversity not as dysfunction, but as the interaction between evolutionary adaptation, developmental variation, and metabolic constraints, producing alternative cognitive architectures with distinct trade-offs. Ultimately, this framework advocates for educational approaches responsive to naturalvariations in cognitive processing, regulation, and learning.
